affectedSurfaces: neutral agent-harness MCP project-config discovery policy
builder merge-conflict resolver and semantic reviewer launches
hypothesis: A neutral fail-closed project-config discovery policy, explicitly set on internal resolver and reviewer launches and enforced before OpenAI-tools MCP manager initialization, prevents an agent-writable worktree from spawning a planted MCP subprocess while preserving explicitly supplied MCP servers.

metricsCompared.name: planted project MCP configurations executed with discovery disabled
metricsCompared.baseline: The OpenAI-tools harness always loaded cwd/.kota/mcp.json before tool restrictions, allowing one planted stdio server fixture to reach subprocess initialization.
metricsCompared.candidate: Zero planted project MCP configurations execute when discovery is disabled; the regression fixture cannot create its subprocess execution marker.

metricsCompared.name: internal merge-conflict launch phases with fail-closed project MCP posture
metricsCompared.baseline: Neither the mutating resolver nor the deny-all semantic reviewer disabled worktree-local MCP discovery.
metricsCompared.candidate: Both resolver and reviewer launch phases explicitly disable project MCP discovery while preserving caller-supplied server declarations at the adapter boundary.

metricsCompared.name: focused security and harness regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: No regression proved that a planted worktree-local MCP configuration could not execute during conflict resolution or review.
metricsCompared.candidate: Eight focused test files pass 50 tests, including policy propagation for both launch phases and the planted execution-marker fixture; typecheck and lint also pass.

rationale: This high-severity Safety repair closes a pre-authorization subprocess launch path at MCP manager initialization. The new policy is explicit and fail-closed only for internal mutable-worktree launches, while the default behavior and explicit session MCP declarations remain available for ordinary operator-selected harness use. Focused tests exercise the previously exploitable boundary and the resolver/reviewer propagation paths without weakening authorization, approval, tool-risk, secret, or injection-defense controls.
